service_at_issue: Home health aide and skilled nursing services exceeding 28/35 weekly hours (NY Medicaid agency appellant)
facts: Before the Council, the appellant argues that the ALJ failed to analyze whether the services furnished to each beneficiary were reasonable and necessary and, therefore, whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services furnished to the beneficiary during the dates of service at issue.

In that regard, the appellant asserts that coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis (seven days a week, but fewer than eight hours each day) or an intermittent basis (six or fewer times a week for as many as 24-hours per day).
outcome_note: The Council dismissed hearing requests for pre-October 1, 2010 dates of service (TPL Demonstration Project waiver) and vacated and remanded the rest because the ALJ erred in denying all coverage solely for exceeding 28/35 weekly hours without analyzing reasonableness and necessity.
